Question: How much drinking water does each person need per day in a flood emergency?
Answer language: English

<doc id="C1" lang="en" title="Water (Ready.gov)" page="1">
[1] Water
[2] Following a disaster clean drinking water may not be available.
[3] Your regular water source could be cut-off or compromised through contamination.
[4] Prepare yourself by building a supply of water that will meet your family's needs during an emergency.
[5] Determining Water Needs
[6] Store at least one gallon of water per person per day for several days, for drinking and sanitation.
[7] A normally active person needs about three quarters of a gallon of fluid daily, from water and other beverages.
</doc>

<doc id="C2" lang="en" title="Build A Kit (Ready.gov)" page="1">
[1] A basic emergency supply kit could include the following recommended items:
[2] • Water (one gallon per person per day for several days, for drinking and sanitation)
[3] • Food (at least a several-day supply of non-perishable food)
[4] • Battery-powered or hand crank radio and a NOAA Weather Radio with tone alert
[5] • Flashlight
[6] • First aid kit
[7] • Extra batteries
[8] • Whistle (to signal for help)
[9] • Dust mask (to help filter contaminated air)
[10] • Plastic sheeting, scissors and duct tape (to shelter in place)
</doc>

Question: سیلاب کی ہنگامی صورتحال میں ہر شخص کو روزانہ کتنا پینے کا پانی چاہیے؟
Answer language: Urdu

<doc id="C1" lang="ur" title="پانی: Ready.gov کا غیر سرکاری اردو ترجمہ" page="1">
[1] پانی (غیر سرکاری اردو ترجمہ)
[2] یہ ترجمہ اسٹچ ٹیم نے امریکی ادارے فیما کی ویب سائٹ ready.gov کے صفحے "Water" سے کیا ہے۔
[3] یہ سرکاری ترجمہ نہیں ہے اور ابھی کسی اہلِ زبان نے اس کی نظرِ ثانی نہیں کی۔
[4] آفت کے بعد پینے کا صاف پانی دستیاب نہ ہونے کا امکان ہوتا ہے۔
[5] پانی کی عام فراہمی بند ہو سکتی ہے یا آلودہ ہو سکتی ہے۔
[6] ہنگامی حالات کے لیے اپنے گھرانے کی ضرورت کے مطابق پانی کا ذخیرہ تیار رکھیں۔
[7] پانی کی ضرورت کا اندازہ
[8] کئی دنوں کے لیے فی شخص روزانہ کم از کم ایک گیلن پانی ذخیرہ کریں، پینے اور صفائی دونوں کے لیے۔
</doc>

<doc id="C2" lang="ur" title="پانی: Ready.gov کا غیر سرکاری اردو ترجمہ" page="1">
[1] ایک عام سرگرم شخص کو روزانہ تقریباً تین چوتھائی گیلن مشروبات کی ضرورت ہوتی ہے، جو پانی اور دوسرے مشروبات سے پوری ہوتی ہے۔
[2] تاہم ہر شخص کی ضرورت عمر، صحت، جسمانی حالت، سرگرمی، خوراک اور موسم کے لحاظ سے مختلف ہوتی ہے۔
[3] • بچوں، دودھ پلانے والی ماؤں اور بیمار افراد کو زیادہ پانی کی ضرورت ہو سکتی ہے۔
[4] • طبی ہنگامی صورت میں اضافی پانی درکار ہو سکتا ہے۔
[5] • گرم موسم میں زیادہ پانی کی ضرورت ہوتی ہے۔
[6] بہت زیادہ گرمی میں پانی کی ضرورت دوگنی ہو سکتی ہے۔
[7] • پینے کے پانی کی راشن بندی نہ کریں جب تک حکام ایسا کرنے کا حکم نہ دیں۔
</doc>

Question: What emergency shelter should be provided to families displaced by floods?
Answer language: English

<doc id="C1" lang="en" title="Field Operations Guide for Disaster Assessment and Response, Version 4.0: food rations and shelter (USAID/OFDA)" page="3">
[1] They are difficult to live in and provide little insulation from temperature extremes.
[2] Tents, however, may be useful for DPs of nomadic origin or when local materials are not available or are only seasonally available.
[3] If tents are used, repair materials should be provided.
[4] The best way to meet emergency shelter needs is to ensure the availability of materials or shelter similar to those normally used by the displaced population or the local population.
</doc>

<doc id="C2" lang="en" title="Field Operations Guide for Disaster Assessment and Response, Version 4.0: food rations and shelter (USAID/OFDA)" page="3">
[1] The key to providing adequate shelter is the roof.
[2] If materials for constructing a complete shelter are inadequate, priority should be given to constructing a roof.
[3] Walls can be made of earth or other materials found onsite location or made locally available.
[4] Housing should meet the cultural and social requirements of the DPs.
[5] Familiar housing will help reduce the disorientation and emotional stress suffered by the displaced population.
[6] To the extent possible, longer term housing must be similar in design and construction to that with which the DPs are familiar, while reflecting local conditions and practice.
</doc>

<doc id="C3" lang="en" title="Field Operations Guide for Disaster Assessment and Response, Version 4.0: food rations and shelter (USAID/OFDA)" page="3">
[1] The covered living space provided should enable separation and privacy between the sexes, between different age groups and between separate families within a given household, as needed.
[2] Further, the space provided should accommodate new or pre-disaster/crisis livelihood activities within the shelter.
[3] Achieving this objective often requires a coordinated effort among donors, NGOs, local and national governments, and affected populations.
[4] Lack of adequate shelter and clothing can have a major adverse effect on the health and nutritional status of displaced people.
</doc>

Question: How long should water be boiled to make it safe to drink?
Answer language: English

<doc id="C1" lang="en" title="Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water (US EPA)" page="1">
[1] • Bring water to a rolling boil for at least one minute.
[2] At altitudes above 5,000 feet (1,000 meters), boil water for three minutes.
[3] • Let water cool naturally and store it in clean containers with covers.
[4] • To improve the flat taste of boiled water, add one pinch of salt to each quart or liter of water, or pour the water from one clean container to another several times.
</doc>

<doc id="C2" lang="en" title="Water (Ready.gov)" page="2">
[1] There are many ways to treat water.
[2] Often the best solution is a combination of methods.
[3] Before treating, let any suspended particles settle to the bottom or strain them through coffee filters or layers of clean cloth.
[4] Boiling
[5] Boiling is the safest method of treating water.
[6] In a large pot or kettle, bring water to a rolling boil for one full minute, keeping in mind that some water will evaporate.
[7] Let the water cool before drinking.
[8] Boiled water will taste better if you put oxygen back into it by pouring the water back and forth between two clean containers.
[9] This also will improve the taste of stored water.
</doc>

Answer language: English

<doc id="C1" lang="en" title="Floods (Ready.gov)" page="1">
[1] If you are under a flood warning
[2] • Find safe shelter right away.
[3] • Do not walk, swim or drive through flood waters.
[4] Turn Around, Don't Drown!
[5] • Remember, just six inches of moving water can knock you down, and one foot of moving water can sweep your vehicle away.
[6] • Stay off bridges over fast-moving water.
[7] • Depending on the type of flooding: evacuate if told to do so, move to higher ground or a higher floor, or stay where you are.

Question: What should people do if they are trapped in a building during a flood?
Answer language: English

<doc id="C1" lang="en" title="Floods (Ready.gov)" page="3">
[1] Turn Around.
[2] Don't Drown!
[3] • Stay off bridges over fast-moving water.
[4] Fast-moving water can wash bridges away without warning.
[5] • Stay inside your car if it is trapped in rapidly moving water.
[6] Get on the roof if water is rising inside the car.
[7] • Get to the highest level if trapped in a building.
[8] Only get on the roof if necessary and once there, signal for help.
[9] Do not climb into a closed attic to avoid getting trapped by rising floodwater.
[10] After a Flood
</doc>

Question: Should children take part in cleanup work after a flood?
Answer language: English

<doc id="C1" lang="en" title="Floods (Ready.gov)" page="3">
[1] Children should not take part in disaster cleanup work.
[2] • Be aware that snakes and other animals may be in your house.
[3] • Be aware of the risk of electrocution.
[4] Do not touch electrical equipment if it is wet or if you are standing in water.
[5] Turn off the electricity to prevent electric shock if it is safe to do so.
[6] • Avoid wading in floodwater, which can be contaminated and contain dangerous debris.
[7] Underground or downed power lines can electrically charge the water.
[8] • Use a generator or other gasoline-powered machinery ONLY outdoors and away from windows.
</doc>

[5] • Use care when handling dry ice.
[6] Wear dry, heavy gloves to avoid injury.

Question: What kind of emergency food supply should a household keep?
Answer language: English

<doc id="C1" lang="en" title="Food (Ready.gov)" page="1">
[1] • Remember any special dietary needs.
[2] We suggest the following items when selecting emergency food supplies.
[3] You may already have many of these on hand.
[4] • Ready-to-eat canned meats, fruits, vegetables and a can opener
[5] • Protein or fruit bars
[6] • Dry cereal or granola
[7] • Peanut butter
[8] • Dried fruit
[9] • Canned juices
[10] • Non-perishable pasteurized milk
[11] • High-energy foods
[12] • Food for infants
[13] • Comfort/stress foods
</doc>

<doc id="C2" lang="en" title="Build A Kit (Ready.gov)" page="1">
[1] Build A Kit
[2] After an emergency, you may need to survive on your own for several days.
[3] Being prepared means having your own food, water and other supplies to last for several days.
[4] A disaster supplies kit is a collection of basic items your household may need in the event of an emergency.
[5] Basic Disaster Supplies Kit
[6] To assemble your kit store items in airtight plastic bags and put your entire disaster supplies kit in one or two easy-to-carry containers such as plastic bins or a duffel bag.
</doc>

<doc id="C3" lang="en" title="Food (Ready.gov)" page="1">
[1] Food
[2] Following a disaster there may be power outages that could last for several days.
[3] Stock canned foods, dry mixes and other staples that do not require refrigeration, cooking, water or special preparation.
[4] Be sure to include a manual can opener and eating utensils.
[5] Suggested Emergency Food Supplies
[6] Consider the following things when putting together your emergency food supplies:
[7] • Store at least a several-day supply of non-perishable food.
[8] • Choose foods your family will eat.
</doc>

<doc id="C4" lang="en" title="Build A Kit (Ready.gov)" page="2">
[1] • Re-think your needs every year and update your kit as your family's needs change.
[2] Kit Storage Locations
[3] Since you do not know where you will be when an emergency occurs, prepare supplies for home, work and cars.
[4] • Home: Keep this kit in a designated place and have it ready in case you have to leave your home quickly.
[5] Make sure all family members know where the kit is kept.
[6] • Work: Be prepared to shelter at work for at least 24 hours.
[7] Your work kit should include food, water and other necessities like medicines, as well as comfortable walking shoes, stored in a "grab and go" case.
[8] • Car: In case you are stranded, keep a kit of emergency supplies in your car.
</doc>

<doc id="C5" lang="en" title="Build A Kit (Ready.gov)" page="1">
[1] A basic emergency supply kit could include the following recommended items:
[2] • Water (one gallon per person per day for several days, for drinking and sanitation)
[3] • Food (at least a several-day supply of non-perishable food)
[4] • Battery-powered or hand crank radio and a NOAA Weather Radio with tone alert
[5] • Flashlight
[6] • First aid kit
[7] • Extra batteries
[8] • Whistle (to signal for help)
[9] • Dust mask (to help filter contaminated air)
[10] • Plastic sheeting, scissors and duct tape (to shelter in place)
</doc>

Answer language: English

<doc id="C1" lang="en" title="Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water (US EPA)" page="3">
[1] Store the settled and filtered water in clean containers with covers.
[2] Other Disinfection Methods
[3] If you don't have liquid bleach, you can use one of the other disinfection methods described below.
[4] Granular calcium hypochlorite.
[5] The first step is to make a chlorine solution that you will use to disinfect your water.
[6] For your safety, do it in a ventilated area and wear eye protection.
[7] Add one heaping teaspoon (approximately 1/4 ounce) of high-test granular calcium hypochlorite (HTH) to two gallons of water and stir until the particles have dissolved.
</doc>

<doc id="C2" lang="en" title="Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water (US EPA)" page="3">
[1] The mixture will produce a chlorine solution of approximately 500 milligrams per liter.
[2] To disinfect water, add one part of the chlorine solution to each 100 parts of water you are treating.
[3] This is about the same as adding 1 pint (16 ounces) of the chlorine solution to 12.5 gallons of water.
[4] If the chlorine taste is too strong, pour the water from one clean container to another and let it stand for a few hours before use.
[5] CAUTION: HTH is a very powerful oxidant.
</doc>

<doc id="C3" lang="en" title="Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water (US EPA)" page="2">
[1] Disinfecting with household bleach
[2] • Disinfect water using household bleach, if you can't boil water.
[3] Only use regular, unscented chlorine bleach products that are suitable for disinfection and sanitization as indicated on the label.
[4] The label may say that the active ingredient contains 6 or 8.25% of sodium hypochlorite.
[5] Do not use scented, color safe, or bleaches with added cleaners.
[6] • If water is cloudy, let it settle and filter it through a clean cloth, paper towel, or coffee filter.
</doc>

<doc id="C4" lang="en" title="Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water (US EPA)" page="2">
[1] • Stir and let stand for 30 minutes.
[2] The water should have a slight chlorine odor.
[3] If it doesn't, repeat the dosage and let stand for another 15 minutes before use.
[4] • If the chlorine taste is too strong, pour the water from one clean container to another and let it stand for a few hours before use.
[5] Amount of bleach to add (bleach may contain 6 or 8.25% sodium hypochlorite):
[6] • 1 quart/liter of water: 2 drops of 6% bleach, or 2 drops of 8.25% bleach.
</doc>

Question: Does boiling water remove heavy metals and other chemicals?
Answer language: English

<doc id="C1" lang="en" title="Water (Ready.gov)" page="3">
[1] Comparison of methods
[2] • Boiling: kills microbes, yes.
[3] Removes other contaminants (heavy metals, salts, and most other chemicals), no.
[4] • Chlorination: kills microbes, yes.
[5] Removes other contaminants, no.
[6] • Distillation: kills microbes, yes.
[7] Removes other contaminants, yes.
</doc>

<doc id="C2" lang="en" title="Water (Ready.gov)" page="3">
[1] If it still does not smell of chlorine, discard it and find another source of water.

[3] Distillation
[4] While boiling and chlorination will kill most microbes in water, distillation will remove microbes (germs) that resist these methods, as well as heavy metals, salts and most other chemicals.
</doc>

[1] Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water
[2] In an emergency situation where regular water service has been interrupted - like a hurricane, flood, or water pipe breakage - local authorities may recommend using only bottled water, boiled water, or disinfected water until regular water service is restored.
[3] The instructions below show you how to boil and disinfect water to kill most disease-causing microorganisms that may be present in the water.
[4] However, boiling or disinfection will not destroy other contaminants, such as heavy metals, salts, and most other chemicals.
</doc>

<doc id="C2" lang="ur" title="خوراک کا راشن اور ہنگامی پناہ گاہ: USAID فیلڈ آپریشنز گائیڈ کا غیر سرکاری اردو ترجمہ" page="2">

[2] مناسب پناہ گاہ کی کنجی چھت ہے۔

[1] بنیادی ہنگامی سامان
[2] ہنگامی سامان کی ایک بنیادی کٹ میں یہ اشیا شامل ہو سکتی ہیں:
[3] • پانی (کئی دنوں کے لیے فی شخص روزانہ ایک گیلن، پینے اور صفائی کے لیے)
[4] • خوراک (کم از کم کئی دنوں کے لیے خراب نہ ہونے والی خوراک)
[5] • بیٹری یا ہاتھ سے چلنے والا ریڈیو
[6] • ٹارچ
[7] • ابتدائی طبی امداد کا سامان
[8] • اضافی بیٹریاں
[9] • مدد کے لیے اشارہ کرنے کی سیٹی
[10] • ذاتی صفائی کے لیے گیلے ٹشو، کچرے کے تھیلے اور پلاسٹک کی ڈوریاں
[11] • ڈبہ کھولنے کا اوزار
[12] • چارجر اور اضافی بیٹری کے ساتھ موبائل فون

[1] ہنگامی پناہ کی ضرورت پوری کرنے کا بہترین طریقہ یہ ہے کہ وہی سامان یا پناہ گاہ دستیاب کی جائے جو بے گھر لوگ یا مقامی آبادی عام طور پر استعمال کرتے ہیں۔

[4] زیادہ بارش والے علاقوں میں فرش اونچا رکھنا ضروری ہے۔

[7] پناہ گاہ کو گرم کرتے وقت خاص احتیاط کی جائے: پلاسٹک کی شیٹ جل سکتی ہے، اس لیے پناہ گاہ کے اندر یا قریب کھلی آگ نہ جلائی جائے۔
